human_tolerance.notes: Authored judgement from the Wikipedia statement that some continental birds winter in gardens in Great Britain and Ireland; no French human-tolerance source was checked.

phases.name: breeding
phases.note: Authored window for France; no sourced French breeding dates were checked. Blackcaps build cup nests in scrub and trees (Wikipedia).

vocalizations.description: Rich musical warbling, often ending in a loud high-pitched crescendo (Wikipedia).
Short alarm call given when disturbed; authored placeholder, no recording or description source checked.

common_names.note: Wikidata labels: fr 'Fauvette à tête noire'. English 'Eurasian blackcap' from the GBIF vernacular name.

range.note: Wikipedia: 'The blackcap breeds in much of Europe, western Asia and northwestern Africa'. The country list is an authored subset of those regions; no western Asian country list was checked, so the list is incomplete for that region.

traits.note: Wikipedia: length about 13 cm; wing length 7-8 cm (wing length is not used as wingspan); typical adult mass 16-25 g; cup nest in cover of bramble, scrub or trees.

traits.mass_kg.note: Midpoint of the Wikipedia range 16-25 g (20.5 g). The mid-point is an authored estimate, not a measured mean.

traits.lifespan_y.note: ex = Ba + (-1/ln(phi)), the BTO-described formula for expected total age given breeding age. Ba = 1 year from Wikipedia (Behaviour > Breeding): 'Blackcaps first breed when they are one year old'. phi = 0.402 from Dryad ELEscholer2020_data.csv row X=845 (Siriwardena et al. 1998; Sylvia atricapilla; United Kingdom; dead recovery; duration 33 years; adult survival per the dataset's usage notes). Result 1 + 1.098 = 2.10 years. Using Wikipedia's adult annual survival of 43% instead gives 2.18. Wikipedia also says 'The typical life expectancy is two years'. Caveat: the formula is conditional on reaching breeding age, so it is not an average over hatchlings, and phi comes from one study.

traits.diet.note: Authored 80/20 split from Wikipedia: 'feeds mainly on insects during the breeding season, then switches to fruit in late summer'. No diet proportion was taken from a source.

traits.social.note: Authored judgement: territorial pairs in the breeding season, solitary birds at other times.

habitat.note: Wikipedia: nest 'built in the cover of bramble, scrubs or trees'. Strata shares, resource weights and urban affinity are authored judgement.

seasonal.note: Strategy PartialMigration from Wikipedia: 'birds from the colder areas of its range winter in scrub or trees in northwestern Europe' while some populations migrate. winter_fraction is NOT set: the validator requires it for PartialMigration and no defensible licensed or France-specific value was found, so the record fails validation (MissingWinterFraction) until a sourced value is supplied. The French breeding window is authored and unsourced.

vocalizations.note: Song description and season from Wikipedia ('rich musical warbling ... loud high-pitched crescendo'). Season months are authored. The alarm call is an authored placeholder, not a sourced description.

behavior.note: Authored program choice: bt-perching-songbird-v1. Only invertebrate food is reachable; the program cannot represent the late-summer fruit switch. Nest months are the program's nest_m1/nest_m2 override, which keeps its fixed 4 and 5 months and so yields April-June.

look.note: Authored judgement: a biped_winged model with a black cap and grey upperparts. Colours and proportions were not sourced from a field guide.
